newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOCUS-Novo first half profit up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Novo first half profit up 10 pct.

text.p: Danish drug group Novo Nordisk on Wednesday reported a 10 percent rise in net profit for the first half of 1997 and repeated a forecast of 15 percent growth in operating income for the full year.
Its six month net profit rose to 960 million crowns, compared with 873 million during the same period last year and the pre-tax result rose to 1.345 billion crowns from 1.229 billion.
The pre-tax figure was above an average forecast of 1.272 billion crowns but although the share price initially jumped to 720.00 crowns from Tuesday's closing 704.00 it later fell back to 715.00.
"The results are somewhat better than expected but there are few real players," a dealer said, adding that the market was in general very thin, magnifying price movements.
The company reported a leap in licence fees and other operating revenues of 53 percent to 310 million crowns, of which 267 million came from licence fees for the antidepressant Seroxat/Paxil.
It added that the increase was partly due to a 20 percent rise in the value of sterling against the crown between the first halves of 1996 and 1997.
Overall costs increased in line with sales, which Novo said it now expected to be lower for the full year than previously foreseen but offset by developments in the yen, dollar and sterling.
It added that it was delaying the launch of its NovoSeven haemophilia treatment in the United States to allow further clinical study urged by the Food and Drug Administration.

"At the request of the FDA a further clinical study will be initiated prior to marketing of NovoSeven in the U.S. Launch of the product is now expected to take place in the first half of 1998," it said.

The statement said that worldwide sales of the treatment amounted to 149 million crowns in the first six months of 1997, almost treble the total of the first half of 1996 when the product was first introduced.
Novo also said that it would change its accounting principles from January 1, 1998, bringing them into line with United States standards.

"These changes, which will result in a higher degree of comparibility between Novo Nordisk's financial statements and those of other international companies....will in all essentials be in harmony with U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles," it said. -- Copenhagen newsroom +(45) 33 969650
